problems.note: Story card 4 says 'The window is glass. Glass is a solid too.' Glass is generally taught as a solid at this grade, but some teachers dispute this because glass is an amorphous solid and the 'glass flows over centuries' myth is common. Consider a short clarifier, such as 'Glass keeps its shape, so it is a solid,' or swap in a clearer solid such as a window frame or a door, so the card doesn't invite that debate.

Only this item shows emoji on its choices (🪨, 🍃, 🌧️). The other items have no pictures. Choice pictures are allowed, but the item is still audio-first, so check that each choice's narration names the object and that the emoji adds no extra meaning a child who can't see the picture would miss.
